title: Sliding-window consumption decay, auto-proration, and shortfall buffer (PRD)
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem statement: Customers changing plans mid-cycle or with spiky consumption frequently see surprising invoices because our current billing model uses a blunt monthly snapshot and simple per-token metering. We need a robust model that: (1) smooths short-term spikes via a sliding-window consumption decay, (2) automatically prorates plan changes and trial conversions in an intuitive, auditable way, and (3) offers a configurable shortfall (debt) buffer to avoid immediate hard cutoffs for enterprise customers while preserving predictable invoicing.

Goals:
- Reduce invoicing disputes related to mid-cycle plan changes by 50% (target metric: invoicing_dispute_rate).
- Provide transparent billing preview in Console that matches invoice line items exactly for 99.9% of beta customers.
- Keep implementation incremental and feature-flagged to allow staged rollouts and quick rollback.

Scope (in):
- Backend metering changes to support sliding-window consumption aggregation for each account and for per-route metrics.
- Deterministic proration algorithm for plan upgrades/downgrades that is timezone-safe and aligns with billing-period boundaries.
- Shortfall buffer configurable per-customer tier (default 72-hour grace and 20% monthly quota buffer for enterprise).
- Console billing preview page updates and billing API endpoints exposing prorated breakdowns.
- E2E acceptance tests and integration with invoicing pipeline (line-item generation).

Scope (out):
- Legacy invoice reconciliation UX (will be handled by a future cleanup PR).
- Complex inter-account credit transfers (covered by cross-account plan in a follow-up).

Key design decisions / algorithm choices:
1) Sliding-window consumption decay: use a 30-day sliding window with exponential decay (half-life = 7 days) applied to token-equivalent consumption. This smooths 1- to 3-day spikes while still reflecting sustained usage. Carryover-calc = sum_{t in window} usage_t * exp(-ln(2) * age_t / 7d). We cap carryover at 20% of the monthly quota to avoid unbounded crediting.
2) Proration for plan changes: prorate based on exact seconds in the billing period that the new plan was active. Example: If a customer upgrades on day 10 at 15:23 UTC, the cost difference is prorated by seconds remaining in billing window; credits from the old plan's unused allowance are converted using the sliding-window-adjusted remaining allowance. Round all monetary calculations to cents using banker's rounding.
3) Shortfall buffer: default enterprise buffer = min(20% of monthly quota, 72 hours of recent average consumption). Buffer consumption is metered but invoiced after a grace period; if buffer is exceeded at end of grace, auto-invoice and optionally trigger alerts. Admins can configure buffer size and grace in Console.

Trade-offs considered:
- Complexity vs. predictability: exponential decay adds computation but produces smoother customer experience. We evaluated linear window and found more abrupt billing changes.
- Rounding and small balances: banker's rounding avoids systematic bias over many customers. We accept small rounding diffs (< $0.01/customer) to reduce implementation complexity.

Rollout plan (high level):
- Phase 0: Backend prototypes, unit tests, and math verification (feature flag off) — ENG 2-week spike.
- Phase 1 (Beta): Enable for 10% of customers (opt-in in Console) and run billing-preview in dry-run mode for two billing cycles. Monitor invoicing_discrepancy_rate and proration_preview_match.
- Phase 2: Gradual 50% rollout with enterprise opt-in for shortfall buffer config.
- Phase 3: General availability with full Console controls and docs.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- invoicing_discrepancy_rate: target < 0.2% post-GA.
- proration_preview_match: target 99.9% match between Console preview and generated invoice line items.
- customer_support_tickets_billing: reduce by 50% vs baseline after 2 months.

Integration points and dependencies: backend metering team (ENG-44321), invoicing pipeline (ENG-55600), Console billing UI (DES-8102), legal for billing terms update (OPS-1910).

Operational considerations:
- All calculations must be reproducible from metering snapshots to allow auditability. Persist intermediate proration deltas (hashable) so Support can reproduce line items.
- Protect against timezone drift by normalizing all plan-change timestamps to UTC on write.

Open questions:
- Should trial-to-paid conversions use the same buffer defaults as enterprise? (PM/Finance to decide by 2025-12-01)
- Do we allow negative rounding small cents to be aggregated monthly and refunded automatically? (Finance preference requested)

Documentation & communications:
- Confluence PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Sliding+Window+Proration+PRD (draft)
- External support KB and billing-preview explainer to be published in Beta phase.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Console billing-preview must show an itemized prorated breakdown that, when sent to the invoicing engine in dry-run, produces identical line items for 99.9% of beta accounts over two billing cycles.
AC-2: Backend metering implements sliding-window decay and exposes an API endpoint /billing/proration-preview that returns deterministic breakdowns for a given timestamp and plan-change history.
AC-3: Rounding rules documented and banker's rounding applied; unit tests cover edge cases (midnight UTC changes, DST irrelevant due to UTC normalization, sub-cent aggregates).
AC-4: Shortfall buffer functionality available for enterprise customers behind feature flag; configured buffer correctly applied per-account and triggers alerts when exceeded after grace period.

AC-5: Performance: preview endpoint responds within 300ms P95 for single-account queries; batch snapshot recompute does not increase nightly billing job duration by more than 20% in staging load tests.
AC-6: End-to-end regression tests covering upgrades, downgrades, trial conversions, and plan-cancel mid-cycle pass in CI.
AC-7: Monitoring dashboards created and alerting thresholds set for invoicing_discrepancy_rate (>0.2%) and proration_preview_match (<99.9%).
AC-8: Finance sign-off on invoice representation and sample invoices for 5 representative customer archetypes (low, bursty startup, steady SaaS, enterprise with buffer, multi-plan org).

rollout_plan: Feature flagged: start with opt-in Beta for 10% of accounts. Dry-run mode will write preview line items to _billing_preview table without emitting invoices for two billing cycles. After metrics validate, enable buffer config for enterprise tenants, then incrementally increase rollout to 50% and GA. Emergency rollback: disable feature flag and re-run nightly billing job to reconcile using legacy snapshot; run customer remediation for any flagged mismatches.
